inputs.xtext_rule_text:
IfNode returns SysML::IfActionUsage :
	ActionNodePrefix 
	'if' ownedRelationship += ExpressionParameterMember
	ownedRelationship += ActionBodyParameterMember
	( 'else' ownedRelationship += ( ActionBodyParameterMember | IfNodeParameterMember ) )?
;

notes: re-scoped from the shared unit to sysml alone (ADR-0015)
decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.17.7. The clause and the Xtext state this production identically, token for token (SysML.xtext:1596), so there is nothing to weigh. The else branch's choice between an ActionBodyParameterMember and an IfNodeParameterMember is what makes `else if` a chain rather than a special form: the second alternative nests another IfNode in the else position, and the clause's own recursion through IfNodeParameterMember is what terminates it.

evidence.note: States the production; the rule is its transcription.

Lines 7-12 exercise both else alternatives in one chain: `if i < 0 {` ... `} else if i == 0 {` takes the IfNodeParameterMember branch, nesting a second IfNode, and `} else {` on line 11 takes the ActionBodyParameterMember branch. Line 15 `if i > 0 {` is the form with no else at all.
Second opinion. Identical to the clause.
